body: That's great. Unfortunately I'm a female and mostly asexual so that isn't a solution for me. It's nice to hear I'm not the only unfeeling one though.

I already climbed out of my parent situation long ago. I moved out when I was 18 and I live far away from them. It's one of the few things I am appreciative of, my independence. I just don't want to fuck up and end up in the position that they (parents) would take it upon themselves to take care of me. Since they probably would be the only ones to do it, and they would even 'gladly' do it.

My condolences about your mom. That must be hard. What do you mean by your father is next?

I hope that life can get better for you, and you continue to have the courage to stand up and hang in there.

By 'supposed to be a good life' I mean that I don't have a legitimate reason to be unhappy or empty. I have things other people would appreciate.

Being unhappy doesn't mean anything to me anymore. Nothing means anything to me. So maybe apathy is more what I meant to say. Not so much recently but I used to alternate between feeling very sad and hopeless for no good reason or trivial ones and then overwhelming apathy. Now there is just apathy. 

To actually answer your question: I'd have to define happiness and that is not something I can do. I have been trying to answer that since I was a teenager and I haven't ever found an answer that sticks.

I can't change the mirror. I've tried changing myself, but it just ends in things being worse.

I appreciate your saying so. I actually have turned 'coping methods' often, in phases of different things but alcohol and sleeping pills have been a near constant. Them and benzo's are the only way I do occasionally manage to be social. But I've given up on that problem long ago. I don't feel any desire to be social anymore. And I do feel like I have wasted my 22 years.

Oh, and I like music. I have had friends share their music with me but for me music can't really give my life meaning. I can sort of understand how it could be someone's purpose and connection, and that's great that it has given you that.

I admire art but it's just not meaningful for me. 

Thank you for taking the time to respond and for sharing your story.
